input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete ("any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") extending 24 months past the term — walk-away territory under this rule (post-term non-compete longer than 12 months and undefined scope), and it also contradicts the pro-Customer confirmation in Section 12.3. No other clause imposes a field-of-use or territory restriction on Customer (Section 13.4 is only ordinary use restrictions; Section 2.2 exclusivity is a separate rule). We take the preferred position by converting 12.4 into an express permission so Customer carries no non-compete or field-of-use restriction, consistent with 12.3; the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, 12 months, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire
ops.newText: Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or businesses we may develop, buy, or sell, so we have removed the 24-month post-term non-compete in Section 12.4, which also contradicted Section 12.3. If the relationship needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Convert Section 12.4 from a 24-month post-term non-compete into an express confirmation that Customer may compete.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
